verbatims: Ooh, Lake Louise frozen in winter, and a brass band walking everyone through New Orleans, that's different. Sending that bit to my partner. Good to know Hawaii is legal for us without hanging around for ages. But I still have no idea if 60 people in Maui is a 40k wedding or a 150k wedding, and the bit for Australian passports basically says google it. Why are we third after Americans and Brits? Saving it, will look properly on the weekend.

verbatims: Okay, the Hawaii licence bit is solid, I'll give them that. Everything else is 'tell us and we'll check'. Rules? We'll check. Seasons? Tell us your month. Cost? It depends on the place, the season, your guests and flights. Yes, I know. Then the places list changes between two sections, Vancouver and Toronto get a card and then disappear, and the FAQ tells me Aussies need authorisation right after another bit told me to go look it up myself. 'Weddings we have featured', so did you plan them or not? And one line says you're with me to the last dance and another says to the guest list. What's the catch? I can't tell, and that's the problem. Closing the tab.

verbatims: OK, the Hawaii bit is actually useful, no waiting period, passport is fine, they link the government page. But I had to scroll a long way on my phone to see 'elopements and small weddings are welcome', and in between it's parades, estate dinners and Gatsby ballrooms. Banff and Vegas just say 'we check'. Nothing about witnesses, nothing about a church wedding, and no idea what the minimum is. Still, they've got 'just the two of you' in the form, so I'll send it and ask.
